summary: The patch adds a MatrixSymbol-only special case to _print_Add, but a bare MatrixSymbol always has coefficient +1, so the new branch never emits a '-' and produces identical output to the old code; the actual negative terms in the issue (`-A*B`, `-B`) are MatMul objects, not MatrixSymbol, so they are not handled at all. The approach cannot resolve the reported bug and is likely non-functional (also risks a NameError if MatrixSymbol is not imported in str.py).

issues.description: Only `isinstance(term, MatrixSymbol)` is special-cased, but the problematic terms `(-1)*A*B` and `(-1)*B` are MatMul, not MatrixSymbol. Those negative-product terms fall through to the else branch and still print as `(-1)*A*B` / `(-1)*B`, so the reported issue (differences of matrix expressions) is not actually fixed.

A bare MatrixSymbol's `as_coeff_Mul()[0]` is always +1, so `< 0` is never true and `t = self._print(as_coeff_Mul()[1])` reprints the same symbol. The new branch is effectively a no-op — wrong abstraction; a correct fix needs coefficient handling on MatMul or a dedicated `_print_MatAdd`.

The diff references `MatrixSymbol` with no import added (only +4 lines shown). If str.py does not already import MatrixSymbol at module scope, `isinstance(term, MatrixSymbol)` raises NameError on every Add print — a broad regression. Import must be verified/added.
`as_coeff_Mul()` is called twice for the same term instead of unpacking once; minor style/efficiency inconsistency with the surrounding code.
